{{Quote|I'd be honored to be mistaken for you—for ''any'' of you.|Col Takbright, to Wedge Antilles|<ref name="Duty Roster" />}}
'''Col Takbright''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] from [[Uquine]] who served as a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. He was known for his short temper, as well as his resemblance to [[Wedge Antilles]]—which led to his being nicknamed '''Fake Wedge''' by his fellow pilots. A member of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], Takbright was present during the [[Battle of Yavin]], though he remained grounded on [[Yavin 4]]'s [[Great Temple|Base One]] due to the Rebellion's [[starfighter]] shortages.

==Biography==
===Early life===
Col Takbright [[Homeworld|hailed]] from [[Uquine]], a placid [[Planet|world]]<ref name="Duty Roster" /> in the [[Colonies]] region of [[the galaxy]].<ref name="RitR">''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]''</ref> The young Takbright watched in increasing agitation as the [[Galactic Empire]] spread across [[the galaxy]], exploiting and destroying planets for [[ore]] and [[fuel]], all the while [[Death|killing]] all opposition to their rule. Eventually, Takbright realized he couldn't spend another day on his homeworld doing nothing; one night, the young man left Uquine with nothing but some [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], a [[duffel bag]], and a vow to avenge those that had been wronged by the Empire.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

===Joining the Rebellion===
Takbright joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], stationed at [[Great Temple|Base One]] on the [[Yavin 4|fourth moon]] of [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]] where he flew [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]]s with [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]]. During this period, Takbright would butt heads with his fellow pilots, particularly [[Puck Naeco]], on account of his hotheaded, verbose nature. The presence of [[Wedge Antilles]], another Red Squadron pilot who resembled Takbright greatly in both voice and appearance, earned the latter the nickname "Fake Wedge", one which Takbright greatly resented.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

By [[1 BBY]], Takbright had distinguished himself flying raids, with his performance praised by [[Red Leader]] [[Garven Dreis]], as well as several patrols and reconnaissance missions. Due to the Rebellion's starfighter constraints, he was unable to participate in the [[Battle of Scarif]] after the last place was given to [[Pedrin Gaul]]; however he hoped to be given a spot in one of the squadron's [[flight]]s for the upcoming [[Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Duty Roster" />

===Battle of Yavin===
{{Quote|That's impossible, ''even'' for a computer.|Col Takbright, to General Dodonna on Yavin 4|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
[[File:DeathStar_plans.png|thumb|left|250px|Takbright (seated left of Skywalker, back row) attended the pilot's briefing, where he voiced his skepticism for the plan]]
As the [[Death Star]] approached, Takbright attended the starfighter pilot briefing presented by [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]]; he would be seated next to [[Luke Skywalker]], a [[Tatooine]] farmboy that had helped in the rescue of [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and provided the schematics for the [[battle station]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> In one of his characteristic outbursts,<ref name="Duty Roster" /> Takbright loudly expressed his skepticism that the station's two-meter [[thermal exhaust port]] could be reliably struck by [[proton torpedo]]es, even with the help of a [[targeting computer]]. Skywalker reassured Takbright that it was indeed possible, citing his targeting of [[womp rat]]s while bush piloting on his homeworld.<ref name="Episode IV" />

After the briefing, Takbright was admonished for his comments by Naeco, before relating Skywalker's optimistic comments to [[John D. Branon]]. In the squadron ready room, Dreis neglected to assign Takbright to one of the squadron's twelve spots, instead giving a spot to Skywalker,<ref name="Duty Roster" /> who had scored an extraordinarily high score on his flight simulation.<ref name="TPtSatFB">''[[A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy]]''</ref> An angry Takbright flew into a fit of rage in the ready room, only to be stopped by Antilles, who urged him to stop pushing his fellow comrades away.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

[[File:Strategy_Center.png|thumb|right|250x250px|Takbright monitored the battle from the Yavin war room]]
Takbright, along with fellow pilots [[Bren Quersey]], [[Elyhek Rue]], and [[Wenton Chan]], watched the action in the [[Yavin rebel base war room|Great Temple's war room]], becoming increasingly unnerved as the rebel pilots began to be killed one-by-one by [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] and [[turbolaser]]s. Eventually, only Antilles, Skywalker, and [[Biggs Darklighter]] were left conducting their [[Meridian trench|trench]] run. After Antilles' [[micro-maneuvering control]]s were rendered inoperative, Takbright urged [[Kelemah]] to get him out of there; however, Antilles would withdraw from the trench.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

After Darklighter was killed, Takbright grew even more worried as Antilles moved to re-enter the trench despite his loss of fine control, a move that would assuredly lead to his death, if only to buy time for Skywalker as he took his shot. However, before this could happen, Skywalker fired his torpedoes into the Death Star, destroying it and saving the rebel base from imminent destruction. Upon the return of the survivors to Yavin, Takbright chose not to join the rest of the ground crew in their ecstatic celebration around Skywalker's landed starfighter; instead, Takbright, with a new appreciation for his fellow pilot's selfless intentions, greeted Antilles and congratulated him for his valiant efforts.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

==Personality and traits==
Col Takbright was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] with brown [[hair]], brown [[eye]]s, and light skin. He was infamous within the Alliance for his short temper; this temper had led to him being abandoned from missions for the team, causing him to lose it even more. Despite this, he was loyal to the Alliance and got on very well with his fellow pilots. Towards the end of the Battle of Yavin, Takbright began to realize that he underappreciated his friends and their morals; he began to greet them with kindness and cheer and congratulated his friends for what they did.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|l tell you my story. I was originally cast as Wedge. I screwed it up, and I got fired — that is the true story. Every actor sometimes gets fired if they screw it up and mine just happened to be on Star Wars!|Colin Higgins|<ref name="RestinPeace">{{SW|url=news/rip-colin-higgins-the-fake-wedgee|text=RIP Colin Higgins, the "Fake" Wedge|archivedate=20250322055837}}</ref>}}
Col Takbright<ref name="Duty Roster" /> first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where he was portrayed by actor [[Colin Higgins]].<ref name="RestinPeace" /> He was first identified by name in "[[Duty Roster]]," a short story penned by ''Star Wars'' perennial [[Jason Fry]] as part of the ''[[From a Certain Point of View]]'' collection, celebrating the 40th anniversary of ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Duty Roster" /> In [[Star Wars Legends]] sources, the character was identified as being [[Wedge Antilles]] (played by [[Denis Lawson]] in the rest of the film), with both actors' lines dubbed by [[David Ankrum]].<ref name="Episode IV" />

Higgins was the actor initially cast as Wedge Antilles. However, he had failed to memorize his line for the scene on Yavin 4<ref name="Star Players">{{InsiderCite|98|Star Players}}</ref> in the briefing room,<ref name="Episode IV" /> instead expecting a production similar to television, where rehearsal was common. Higgins struggled during the shoot and grew increasingly nervous and dispirited; he was fired after one day and was replaced by Lawson.<ref name="Star Players" /> Higgins' scene, however, remained in the final film.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Before the establishment as Takbright as his own character,<ref name="Duty Roster" /> the character in the briefing room scene was considered Antilles<ref name="RestinPeace" /> despite the visual difference,<ref name="Episode IV" /> but Antilles' appearance in the scene, incongruous with that of the rest of the film, led to a fan nickname of "Fake Wedge." [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member and author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] was responsible for identifying the actor's name and background in [[2004]].<ref name="Mystery">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-mysteries-hunting-for-the-fake-wedge|series=Star Wars Mysteries|text=Hunting for the Fake Wedge}}</ref>

The unofficial fan nickname for Higgins' portrayal was recognized and introduced into [[canon]] by Jason Fry in "Duty Roster," the same story that established "Fake Wedge" as his own character.<ref name="Duty Roster" /> ''[[Star Wars]]'' actor [[Gerald Home]] stated that Higgins had been embarrassed to be considered the "fake" version of a character and made sure to praise him as an excellent actor. Believing that Higgins deserved credit for helping to establish an iconic character like Antilles, [[Mark Newbold]] posted an obituary for Higgins on [[StarWars.com]] on [[May 2]], [[2013]], having learned of Higgins' passing in [[December]] [[2012]] from Home.<ref name="RestinPeace" />
